description:
FILED s473h (Opus, 2026-09-08) as the owner of ir-conform case 272-sort,
taken over from #1249(6).  The brief said: "size it, ship if it is one flag on
literal BOXES with a check on the write path that costs nothing on the hot
path (measure), else file."  MEASURED; it is not that, and this is why.

THE MEASUREMENT (scratch/s473h/probe/m6.pl + m6b.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at
a9f2a264).  perl dies "Modification of a read-only value attempted" in 8 of
the 18 foreach/@_ shapes; PCL modifies in all 18:

  DIES in perl, MODIFIES in PCL            AGREE (both modify)
  ---------------------------------        ------------------------------
  for my $x (1,2)          { $x++ }        for my $x (map {$_} "a")
  for my $x ("a","b")      { $x.="!" }     for my $x (@a)        (variables)
  for my $x (qw(a b))      { $x.="!" }     for my $x (sort @a)
  for my $x (sort "b","a") { $x.="!" }     for my $x (sort split(/,/,$s))
  for my $x (sort 2,1)     { $x++ }        for my $x (1..3)
  for my $x (reverse "b","a")              for my $x (sort {â¦} keys %h)
  for my $x (grep {1} "a")                 for my $x (sort {â¦} grep {1} @g)
  for (1,2) { $_++ }   ($_ spelling)       for my $x (reverse sort {â¦} @rv)
  sub { $_[0] .= "!" }->("a")

  Per ELEMENT, not per list (probed): in `for my $x ("a", $v)` the SECOND
  element IS writable and the first is not.
  `map` returns a COPY and is writable; `sort`, `reverse` and `grep`
  PROPAGATE the read-onlyness of what they alias.

WHY "a flag on literal boxes" DOES NOT EXIST HERE.  In PCL a literal in a
foreach list is a RAW value in the emitted `(vector "a" "b")`, not a box;
%p-foreach-elt's `(t â¦)` arm then PROMOTES it in place (%p-elem-cell) and the
loop variable aliases a fresh writable cell.  So:

  * there is no box to carry the flag at the moment it would have to be set;
  * the raw-vs-boxed distinction cannot stand in for literal-vs-variable â
    under raw element storage a REAL array's elements are raw too, and the
    promoting arm exists precisely for them (boxed-aggregates design Â§4.4);
  * a per-LIST mark would be wrong for `("a", $v)`, which perl treats per
    element.

WHAT IT WOULD ACTUALLY TAKE (three parts, none of them one line):
  1. the COMPILER marks the literal ELEMENTS of a list it builds (the
     emitter knows which are literals â `(vector "a" $v)` already
     distinguishes them by shape, so the mark can be a distinct constructor
     for the literal slots rather than a runtime type test);
  2. a read-only representation the aliasing binder recognises, so
     %p-foreach-elt refuses to promote it and %p-readonly-modification fires
     instead (that fatal and its message already exist, from #159);
  3. PROPAGATION through the aliasing operators â sort / reverse / grep pass
     it along, map does not â and through `@_` for a literal argument.
     Part 3 is the open-ended one.

COST QUESTION not yet answered: whether the check can sit only in the
promoting arm (%p-foreach-elt / the @_ binder), which is not the scalar-write
hot path, or whether it must reach box-set.  If part 1 marks the slot, the
check is at the BINDER and box-set never sees it â that is the design worth
trying first, and it is the reason this is filed rather than declared
impossible.

DIRECTION OF THE DIVERGENCE: PCL is more PERMISSIVE.  Every affected program
is one perl refuses to run, so no working program is mis-answered; what is
lost is the diagnostic.  That is why it is not urgent.

CORPUS: ir-conform/known-fail.tsv row `272-sort` re-pointed from 1249 to this
task.  MEASURED: the case's other five lines (keys2 / grep / reverse /
assign-copy / join) all match perl byte for byte already
(scratch/s473h/probe/m6c.pl) â the ONLY divergence is the missing die at
`for my $x (sort ("b","a"))`, plus the exit code that follows from it
(#1247, exit 255 vs 0).

RELATED, and NOT this task: `@_` aliasing of a VARIABLE argument
(`sub { $_[0] .= "!" }->($v)` leaves $v unchanged in PCL, "b!" in perl) is the
separately ruled `@_`-aliasing non-support in docs/not-supported.md.


=== s497b (2026-09-26): the DIRECT literal half is DONE ===
A literal in the list form of the PROMOTING foreach (p-foreach; p-foreach-raw never writes) is wrapped at MACROEXPANSION in a read-only box (%p-ro-box: a magic cell whose setter is %p-readonly-modification) â lone literal, (vector â¦), (p-flatten-args (list â¦)); no emission change.  chop/chomp now write through box-set (so the setter fires, and a tied $_ is honoured â local.t's three Underscore rows).  `$x = $x` on a magic box is a no-op (perl's sv_setsv(sv, sv); closure.t row 267).  Probe scratch/s497b/p-ro.pl: 18 shapes identical to perl incl. the writable ones (range, array, variable, map).  Rows: ref.t 220-223, tr.t 248, fatals battery x3.  STILL OPEN: propagation through sort / reverse / grep (ir-conform 272-sort).


=== RESIDUE (Fable review s499 of s497b's 91cfcfc0, appended by the s497b resume agent) ===
Four more read-only shapes that LIVE in PCL where perl 5.40.3 dies "Modification of a read-only value attempted":
    my $r = \1; $$r = 2;                          # a ref to a literal
    for ("a") { s/z/x/ }                           # s/// on a read-only alias dies even with NO match
    use constant K => 7; for my $x (K) { $x = 1 }  # a constant sub's value is read-only
    map { $_++ } (1, 2);  grep { $_++ } (1, 2);    # literal aliasing in map/grep
Reproducers: /home/bernt/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/review/q497-readonly.pl rows 6, 8, 13, 24, 28 (outputs under out/).

=== s500a (Opus, 2026-09-30): Scalar::Util::readonly -- the "cheap half" is NOT cheap (measured) ===
perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s500a/probes/sutil.pl row 7/8/9): readonly("lit") 1, readonly(5) 1, readonly(undef) 1, readonly($x) 0, readonly($n) 0, readonly($x . "a") 0; through @_ ro("lit") 1, ro($x) 0, ro(3 + 4) 0; `for my $e ("lit", $x) { readonly($e) }` 1 then 0.
WHY NO RUN-TIME TEST CAN ANSWER ROW 7: the caller's emission is `(pl-readonly "lit")`, `(pl-readonly (p-. $x "a"))` and `(pl-readonly $x)` where `$x` was bound `:scalar` RAW by the VarAnnotator -- all three reach the callee as the same kind of raw CL string.  Only the COMPILER knows which argument was a literal.
WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: a literal ARGUMENT of a user-sub call passed as a read-only box -- a `(load-time-value (%p-ro-box "lit"))` per call site, so no allocation per call -- which is also perl's `sub { $_[0] .= "!" }->("a")` die (this task's @_ row).  That is a call-convention change for every call with a literal argument (raw-params fast path receives a box; corpus-wide emission change; bench it), not a Scalar::Util fix.  Row 9 (the foreach alias of a literal) is reachable today through the s497b %p-ro-box, but shipping row 9 alone would still answer readonly("lit") 0, so nothing was shipped.  not-supported.md has the entry.
subject: A LITERAL is not read-only: `for my $x (sort "b","a") { $x .= "!" }` modifies where perl dies "Modification of a read-only value attempted" -- 8 of 18 shapes measured; needs per-VALUE read-only, not a flag on literal boxes (literals are not boxes in PCL).  Owner of ir-conform 272-sort, from #1249(6)
